submission.natural_language_explanation: N1215+ is a retrospective 'concrete-thing' detector: it fires on the token that completes a word naming a tangible thing - an object, part, material, substance or named type (coating, sills, clumps, ink, mead, fan, phrase, door, crown) - and it reads the word at its final piece only ('ills' in sills, 'ification' in Notification, 'ad' in mead fire at 1.2-1.7 while the preceding ' s', 'Not' and ' me' stay at or below zero), whereas abstract, relational and hedged vocabulary (theory, method, plan, policy, later, likely, implication, guideline, risk) stays inactive. It is lexically selective inside the concrete class (fan, ink, door and mead fire; lamp, table and house do not), and its output direction is anti-aligned with its input key (cos(w_in, w_out) = -0.47), so the unit registers a named concrete referent and damps the vocabulary it has just detected.

The review meeting began with an hour of procedural discussion. The chair explained that the schedule had been revised twice since the spring, that the assumptions behind the forecast were provisional, and that the methodology used to weigh competing priorities would be published later. Members raised questions about the policy on overtime, about the likely implications for staffing, and about whether the criteria were consistent with the guidance issued last year. Nobody could say with confidence which proposals would qualify, and the committee agreed to revisit the matter once further analysis was available.

A second hour passed on the question of how the budget should be divided between maintenance and new construction. The finance officer argued that the estimates were too uncertain to support any commitment, while the operations lead insisted that delay would be more expensive than action. The disagreement was not resolved. By the time the meeting ended, the agenda had grown longer than the minutes, and the action items had been assigned to people who were not present.

The following week, the same questions returned in a different form. A working group was formed to examine the assumptions behind the forecast. Its report described three scenarios, each of which depended on assumptions that could not be tested. The first assumed that demand would remain stable; the second assumed a gradual decline; the third assumed that the policy would be revised within the year. None of the scenarios was judged more likely than the others. The group recommended that the committee adopt a flexible approach, revisit the criteria in six months, and avoid any commitment that could not be reversed. The recommendation was accepted without much discussion.

Within a month, the process had generated more process.
